02.r: States the rule for the future in the land.
02.n: Literally 'there shall not be to the priests', the usual Hebrew way of saying 'the priests shall not have'. The verse opens with this verb, ahead of the people it concerns.

03.r: Those who serve at the altar.
03.n: Literally 'to the priests'; counted here as the subject of 'shall have'.

04.r: Names the priests by their tribe.
04.n: Set beside 'the priests' to describe them: 'the priests, (that is) the Levites'. The DRC reads 'the priests and Levites', the Geneva 'the Priests of the Leuites'.

05.r: Extends the rule from the priests to the whole tribe.

06.r: Levi as a tribe among the tribes.
06.n: BDB: rod, staff, club, sceptre; tribe, and gives מַטֶּה, the other Hebrew word for 'tribe' (also first a staff), as a synonym.

07.r: The ancestor of the tribe set apart for the sanctuary.

08.r: A piece of the land like the other tribes received.
08.n: BDB: portion, tract, territory, of land. The KJV, Geneva and DRC say 'part'.

09.n: After the negative, 'and' works like 'nor': the tribe has neither.

10.r: Levi is not counted with the other tribes in the share-out.

11.r: The other tribes of the nation.

12.r: The sacrifices given to the LORD on the altar, from which the priests take their share.
12.n: Gesenius: a sacrifice, so called from the fire by which it is burned. The brief's lexicon gives 'food offering, offering given to God by fire or eaten by priests'.
t: the offerings of ... made by fire
the offerings of ... made by fire
the offerings of ... made by fire
the offerings of ... made by fire

13.r: The personal name of Israel's God.

14.r: What belongs to the LORD is what the priests live on.
14.n: 'His' most likely refers to the LORD: what is given to him becomes the tribe's food, as the JPS capital and the YLT 'even His inheritance' read it. The BSB takes it as Levi's ('their inheritance'). The DRC has 'his oblations'.

15.r: The offerings are the priests' food in place of the harvest of their own fields.
15.n: The verb ends with an extra syllable (a paragogic nun), a fuller, often emphatic form. That the food takes the place of crops from their own land is a reasonable reading of the verse as a whole.

_extra.20: αὐτά (them): the Greek supplies an object for 'eat', which the Hebrew leaves to be understood.

04.n: The brief marks the dictionary form as loose.

08.n: μερίς, portion, the Greek word our register renders 'portion'.

09.n: οὐδὲ κλῆρος, 'nor a lot': κλῆρος is a share assigned by lot. English 'clergy' comes from this word, by way of Latin.

12.n: κάρπωμα, an offering; the Greek word is formed from καρπός, fruit, and has nothing of the Hebrew's 'fire' in it.

14.n: ὁ κλῆρος αὐτῶν, 'their lot': the Greek takes 'his' as the priests' share, as the BSB does.
